q: What is the key difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
options: A chatbot runs on a schedule
An agent acts on an instruction and works through steps to produce something
explanation: A chatbot waits for a prompt, replies and stops. An agent takes an instruction and keeps going — checking sources, running steps and reporting back — which is why it is described as a prompt plus tools plus steps.

q: Which of these tasks is safest to hand to an agent first?
options: Sending a payment to a supplier
Drafting a weekly summary of your own team's data
Emailing a client without your review
Storing your passwords for quick access
explanation: Drafts and summaries are work you would check anyway, so any error gets caught at review. Money movements, passwords and messages sent without review are on the 'do not hand over yet' list.

q: Why is a wrong number more dangerous inside an agent's finished report than in a single chat reply?
options: Agents are less accurate than chatbots
The error is buried deeper in a whole product built on top of it
Agents run faster, so errors multiply
explanation: If a chatbot gives you a wrong number, you spot it. If an agent builds a whole report on that wrong number, the error is buried deeper — which is why the rule is 'start supervised, stay supervised'.
